note: A2 in data/suite_classification.json means 'buildable and verifiable', NOT 'advised'. These nine tasks were classified A2 by keyword; this file records the engineering verdict after investigation.

712.name: Raft for coordination
712.trigger: ledger must survive host loss or have more than one writer
712.why: majority 2 of 3 is achievable; crash-fault model matches the deployment

713.name: Paxos for agreement
713.why: Raft covers the same ground with fewer ways to be subtly wrong; building both is duplicate work

714.name: complete consensus suite
714.why: umbrella task; the audit document is its index

715.name: HotStuff
715.why: needs >=7 replicas for f=2 plus threshold signatures; no BLS/ed25519 crate exists and n=3 gives f=0

716.name: asynchronous consensus
716.why: safety under asynchrony requires 3f+1 replicas and reliable broadcast; f=0 here so the property cannot be exercised

717.name: randomized consensus
717.why: a termination mechanism for an async BFT protocol that does not exist

718.name: complete consensus testing
718.why: harness over the real decision path (partition 3 peers, kill the kernel mid-proposal) is the only thing that makes the current claim checkable

719.name: consensus optimization
719.why: nothing real to optimise; optimising a vote counter is meaningless
